brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Full bases piece:1,0,0/1,0,1 and piece:2,0,0/2,0,1 with top covers cover:1,0,1 and cover:2,0,1 make a shelf top 310 × 227 mm across; a row of books (prop:1) stands on it.
drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:1#0,0#cut sit in the open cut faces of the stacked half bases piece:0,0,0 and piece:0,0,1.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only, not strength or load. It can't rate the unit for any weight; that depends on the print material and settings and needs testing.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey shelf unit with two drawers, but nothing here can be rated for 50 kg. The left column is two stacked north-half bases with a drawer in each one's open cut face. Next to it stand two columns of full bases, two storeys high, with top covers that make a 310 × 227 mm shelf top; a row of books is shown standing on it. I added edge caps and joint bolts (lockJoints). capOpenFaces as a single op was refused because a cap would clash with a drawer frame, so I fitted 24 caps one by one. Two faces next to the drawer frames are left uncapped for the same reason. The meshes check clear with no rule errors. That comes to 68 parts, above the usual limit of about 40, almost all of them caps. The configurator checks fit only, so the 50 kg rating can't be met: load capacity depends on the print material and settings and needs real testing.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
